templates.name: Annual operating budget
templates.summary: For an owner or finance lead preparing next year: revenue and costs by month and by team, built from this year's figures and each budget owner's drivers, every assumption written down, capital purchases listed apart, the whole checked against cash, and the questions leadership has to settle.

templates.name: Audit preparation
templates.summary: Before the external auditors arrive, your controller holds one audit pack: every request with its owner, date, document and status, the control evidence they will test, last year's findings and what was done, and draft answers to the questions they will ask. People approve everything before it goes.

templates.name: Bank reconciliation preparation
templates.summary: Before the month is signed off, your bookkeeper holds one bank reconciliation for one account: every statement line matched to the books or explained, every open item aged, a proof that the two balances agree, and the entries still to make. Nothing is posted until a person approves.

templates.name: Budget-versus-actual variance commentary
templates.summary: Before the month's results go to management, the finance lead gets written commentary on every line that moved past the threshold: the figures, the budget owner's explanation marked confirmed or to be confirmed, a bridge from budget to actual, and the questions still open. No cause is invented.

templates.name: Collections call brief
templates.summary: Before you phone a customer about overdue invoices, one page sets out every open invoice and its age, what they were told and promised, any dispute or credit note still open, who to ask for and the questions to settle. After the call, what was agreed is written up for a person to confirm.

templates.name: Creator commission statement
templates.summary: Each month, the finance lead gets a draft statement of what every creator has earned, worked from the store's orders export: commission under the programme's rules, flat fees, amounts carried under the minimum, and a payout list. A person approves it; finance pays.

templates.name: Investor update
templates.summary: Each month or quarter, the founder gets a drafted update for investors: the headline, key figures against plan and last period, cash and runway, wins, problems told plainly with what is being done, and specific asks. Every figure comes from the company's own reports. The founder approves and sends it.

templates.name: Job cost review at completion
templates.summary: When a job closes, the controller gets one review that sets recorded labour, material, subcontract and overhead beside the estimate by cost code, shows each difference and what the job-cost records say about it, and lists the questions for the estimator and the job lead. Nothing is changed.

templates.name: Journal entry preparation
templates.summary: At month end, your bookkeeper hands the controller every proposed journal entry ready to review: balanced lines on accounts from your own chart, the arithmetic and the document behind each amount, whether it reverses, and who approves it. Nothing is posted until a person approves.

templates.name: Month-end close checklist
templates.summary: Before the month ends, your controller holds the whole close on one page: every task with its owner, its date and what it waits on, the chain that sets the close date, and each gap already written as a question. Entries are prepared for approval, never posted.

templates.name: Overdue-invoice follow-up preparation
templates.summary: Every overdue invoice gets a follow-up drafted in your firm’s tone for its age and addressed from the right person, and every invoice that should not be chased is held with the reason written down.

templates.name: Payroll preparation and timesheet review
templates.summary: Before each payroll run, the owner gets one sheet built from the timesheet and roster exports: hours by person and type, every missing punch and odd entry raised as a question, and an estimated total. Nothing is keyed in, submitted or paid until a person approves.

templates.name: Payroll register to ledger reconciliation
templates.summary: At period end, the accountant or controller gets one worksheet proving the payroll register against the ledger: gross pay, employer taxes, deductions and net pay. Every difference is sorted as timing, miscoding or unexplained, with a question for each. Nothing is posted.

templates.name: Price change review
templates.summary: Before prices change, the owner or finance lead gets one review: the margin on each product or service from the sales and cost exports, how costs have moved, what each proposed price does to sales and gross profit across a stated range of customer responses, and dated competitor prices. It recommends no price.

templates.name: Receivables exception review
templates.summary: The controller gets every short payment, unmatched or ambiguous receipt, possible duplicate and disputed invoice on one list, each with its evidence and a proposed next step, before anything is applied on a guess.

templates.name: Spreadsheet check before sharing
templates.summary: Before a model or schedule goes to a client, a lender or a board, the sender gets one report on it: every error value, short total, buried assumption and hidden row pinned to its cell, each with a fix or a question, and a plain list of what was not checked. Nothing in the workbook is changed.

templates.name: Supplier bill review and payment-run preparation
templates.summary: Before each payment run, the person who approves it gets one sheet: every supplier bill checked against its purchase order and what was received, duplicates and changed bank details stopped, credits shown, and a proposed run with its total. Nothing is paid until a person approves.

templates.name: Thirteen-week cash flow forecast
templates.summary: The owner sees cash week by week for the next thirteen weeks: what comes in, what goes out, the lowest point and every week below the floor they set, with each assumption written on the page. The forecast informs the decision; the owner makes it, and nothing is paid or moved.

templates.name: Weekly receivables summary
templates.summary: The finance lead takes one page into each week’s management meeting: what came in, where every receivable stands, which exceptions are open and who owns them, and the decisions management must make. Every figure ties to the aging report.

templates.name: Year-end tax packet for the accountant
templates.summary: Once the year's books are closed, the owner or bookkeeper hands the accountant one packet: the documents asked for and what is still missing, every contractor paid over the reporting line with missing tax forms flagged, the year's estimated tax payments, and the questions to ask. It works out no tax.
